title: ～といい／～たらいい — “I hope ～ / you should ～”
summary: Verb + といい / たらいい has two main uses. Speaking about something outside your control, it expresses a hope (“I hope ～”). When talking to someone about what they should do, it gives advice (“you should ～”).

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形／ない形 ＋ といい
patterns.gloss: dictionary or ない form + といい: hope (晴れるといい)
ta-form + ら + いい: advice or suggestion (聞いたらいい)

patterns.form: 〜といいですね／〜といいのですが
patterns.gloss: …といいですね / …といいのですが: polite hope

body.p: Used for things you cannot control, such as weather, results, or deliveries: 明日晴れるといいですね. The speaker is wishing. A softened ending like ～のですが makes the hope more polite.
Used when talking to someone who is in trouble: 道に迷ったら、駅の人に聞いたらいいですよ. It means “it would be good if you did ～.” Both the ta-form + ら and と are possible, but advice is most natural with たら.
With advice to a superior, ～たらいいですよ may sound forward; ～てみてはいかがですか is softer. ～といい for a hope never describes your own deliberate action.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）晴（は）れるといいですね。
examples.romaji: Ashita hareru to ii desu ne.

examples.ja: 週末（しゅうまつ）までに荷物（にもつ）が届（とど）くといいのですが。
examples.romaji: Shūmatsu made ni nimotsu ga todoku to ii no desu ga.
examples.tr: I hope the package arrives by the weekend.

examples.ja: 道（みち）に迷（まよ）ったら、駅（えき）の人（ひと）に聞（き）いたらいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Michi ni mayottara, eki no hito ni kiitara ii desu yo.
examples.tr: If you get lost, you should just ask someone at the station.

pitfalls: For a hope, use things outside your control. For your own plan, say ～たい or ～つもりだ instead.
Advice is たら. Using 聞くといいですよ is possible, but 聞いたらいい is more typical for a direct suggestion.
